svg.title: Idea T4: a cached static map plus a small mover map (not built)
svg.desc: With a sun that does not move, the static casters' map is drawn once and kept, static-on-static shadow is baked at load, and the static receivers' bands are cut once. Each frame only the movers get a small map, cut to the tiles they cover. Three compares give static on mover, mover on static, and mover on mover; a pixel is in shadow where either map says so. Not built: every number is an estimate or open, except the measured anchors from other passes.
svg.text: Idea T4: a cached static map plus a small mover map
NOT BUILT. ESTIMATE / OPEN. The owner's idea for a sun that does not move. The only MEASURED numbers come from the c4 passes, not from this design.
Once, at load (the sun is fixed)
Every frame
Static casters drawn from the sun once:
the static map, kept in video memory
(the c4 map pass, run one time) · used by compare 1
Static on static: baked into vertex colours
or a lightmap. Costs nothing per frame.
Static receivers cut into bands once
(their depth codes do not change) · compare 2
Movers drawn from the sun into a small mover map,
rendered through only the tiles they cover · compares 2, 3
For scale: the full c4 map cut to 20 tiles took 375 us
[MEASURED PVR-092, the c4 map, not a mover map]
Movers cut into bands (their depth codes change
with every step), as in the c4 mask pass today · compares 1, 3
Three compares into the mask, every frame
1 static on mover: the mover's bands against the static map
2 mover on static: the static bands against the mover map
3 mover on mover, self: mover bands against mover map
reads the cached map: no map pass for it this frame
the static bands are sent again, but not cut again
the same as today's chain, on fewer polygons
Join: shadow where either map says so
All three compares write the one 320 x 240 mask; then
the screen layer as in the c4 chain.
Today each band writes with blend ONE / ZERO, which
replaces the pixel. A join needs a write that never
clears a set shadow bit. How: [OPEN]
(the punch-through route of PVR-065 is one candidate, not built)
The catches
1. The PVR's depth buffer stays on chip per tile; no register writes it to memory [FACT PVR-083]. So the static map cannot
be preloaded as the starting depth of the movers' map. Two maps mean two compares, not one.
2. Each extra pass adds waits: the c4 frame was 39.9 ms for 19 – 22 ms of measured work [MEASURED PVR-094]; why [OPEN Q53].
3. How many movers before this costs more than one full map each frame: [OPEN].
Test that would settle it: after c4b works [Q56] and the wait test is done [Q53], time one static map plus one
mover map against the single full map, by pvr_get_stats and the frame time, on the console.
Source: wiki/shadows/bump-compare-chain.md, "Idea: a cached static map plus small mover maps"; open-questions.md T4.
